blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Moving object segmentation is conventionally formulated at the sequence and object level, marking an entire instance as moving once it moves anywhere in a video. Recent instantaneous formulations distinguish moving from stationary intervals, but still generate masks at the object level through frozen segmentation foundation models. Because the mask is derived from an instance-level proposal, motion is typically attributed to the entire instance rather than localized to the regions that actually move. Moreover, such instance-level predictions can produce masks even when no part of the instance is actually moving, revealing a more fundamental issue: motion is not an intrinsic property of an instance; it can only be determined by comparing at least two frames. Building on this premise, we introduce MoRSe, which jointly interprets two frames to predict a moving-region mask, distinguishing actual scene motion from apparent motion induced by the camera. A single RGB encoder replaces multi-stage foundation stacks, so no optical flow, point tracks, or separate mask generator is needed at inference. We release MoRSe-5K, a benchmark of 42 sequences with Static, Dynamic-Static, and Dynamic settings designed to evaluate the model's ability to distinguish and localize moving and stationary regions under different camera and scene motion conditions. MoRSe outperforms both specialized moving object segmentation methods and dense 4D reconstruction methods with motion-thresholded predictions, while producing the fewest false positives on sequences where nothing moves.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Separating independently moving regions from camera-induced image motion is a
core problem in dynamic scene understanding. It prevents dynamic
correspondences from corrupting structure from motion and SLAM, and provides
physically grounded signals for 4D reconstruction. Whether a region is moving
cannot be determined from its appearance alone: the same object may be
stationary for one frame pair and moving for another, while a static wall may
appear to move when the camera moves.

motion as a property of an object rather than of a frame pair. Many video
segmentation datasets label an object throughout a
sequence once it moves at any time, so an appearance model can label a
stationary instance as moving. GMOS takes an important step toward
instantaneous evaluation by annotating moving and stationary intervals ( Xie et al., 2026 ) , but couples motion reasoning to a frozen SAM2 encoder and
an object-level motion head, which can introduce false positives for visible
but stationary objects.

Existing methods usually follow one of two pipelines. Some estimate motion
with optical flow or point tracks and then use a segmentation model to complete
the mask. Geometry explains camera motion, while the segmentation stage
recovers object extent ( Xie et al., 2024b ; Xie et al., 2024a ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Goli et al., 2025 ; He et al., 2026 ) . Errors can accumulate across
correspondence, prompting, and mask propagation. Other methods reconstruct
dense 4D motion and obtain a mask by thresholding the predicted displacement.
Feed-forward 4D models predict per-pixel motion in world coordinates that
already absorb camera motion ( Karhade et al., 2026 ; Luo et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026a ; Liu et al., 2026 ; Qian et al., 2026 ) ,
but a single displacement threshold must handle very different cases, such as a
distant vehicle and a nearby moving limb.

MoRSe ( Mo ving- R egion Se gmentation)
directly predicts a moving-region mask for each source coordinate by attending

not used to build the mask: we do not warp features, subtract a rigid flow, or
threshold a geometric residual (Section 3.2 ).

Motion labels are therefore conditional on the observations rather than
attached to an object once for an entire clip. This lets one source frame
probe three capabilities along separate axes: temporal sensitivity, by varying
the target; spatial localization, by responding only where an instance actually
moves; and robustness to egomotion, by staying silent when apparent
displacement is fully explained by the camera. Camera motion thus becomes a
measurable negative case rather than an artifact absorbed into a
sequence-level label, motivating the benchmark and model below.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are as follows: • We formulate motion on an ordered source–target pair and decode each
source coordinate using target-conditioned attention, without flow, point
tracks, or a segmentation foundation model at inference. A single target
gives an instantaneous region, while a target window gives a long-term
region through a union over targets; a promptable segmenter can recover
whole moving objects (Sections 3.1 , 3.4 ). • We construct and will release MoRSe-5K: 42 sequences and 5,431
frames whose Static, Dynamic-Static, and Dynamic settings evaluate distinct
model capabilities along separate axes. The Static setting has empty ground
truth throughout, allowing ego-motion false positives to be measured
directly—a failure mode that sequence-level MOS benchmarks do not express
(Section 4.2 ). • On MoRSe-5K, MoRSe performs best on moving-region segmentation
and remains competitive on conventional sequence-level MOS benchmarks
outside its target formulation (Section 4.4 ).

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Flow- and Track-Based Segmentation
blocks.zh: 2.1 流量和轨距

blocks.en:
Moving object segmentation (MOS) identifies objects that move in a video; in
the single-foreground setting it becomes a binary motion-segmentation problem
similar to ours. It differs from unsupervised video object segmentation
(UVOS), which targets salient foreground objects. The two tasks share
benchmarks such as DAVIS ( Perazzi et al., 2016 ) , whose sequence-level labels
can reward appearance shortcuts. GMOS adds frame-level moving/static states
and false-positive penalties ( Xie et al., 2026 ) , but uses a frozen geometric
encoder ( Wang et al., 2026 ) , frozen SAM2 features, an object-level head, and
mask propagation; its binary GMOS-S variant retains this design. We instead
condition the mask on an ordered source–target pair. Other MOS systems first
obtain motion proposals and then complete them with a segmenter: FlowSAM uses
flow with SAM ( Xie et al., 2024b ) , Appearance-Based Refinement corrects
incomplete masks ( Xie et al., 2024a ) , and SegAnyMo prompts SAM2 from
long-term point trajectories ( Karazija et al., 2024 ; Huang et al., 2025 ; Ravi et al., 2025 ) .
Our model learns pair-conditioned evidence and mask prediction jointly.

blocks.en: 2.2 Geometric Motion Reasoning
blocks.zh: 2.2 几何运动

blocks.en:
Geometric methods test whether correspondences agree with a static scene under
camera motion. RoMo fits a per-video classifier to flow-based epipolar
residuals ( Goli et al., 2025 ) ; the cue is interpretable but requires robust
fitting and test-time adaptation and is less reliable under pure rotation or
low parallax. Easi3R derives dynamic cues from cross-view attention in a
pretrained reconstruction model ( Chen et al., 2025 ) , while VGGT4D reads
attention maps from a frozen VGGT ( Wang et al., 2025 ) without extra training ( Hu et al., 2026 ) . These cues were learned for reconstruction, so a
separate statistic is needed to obtain a mask. GeoMotion combines latent
geometry, appearance, and precomputed flow ( He et al., 2026 ) ; MegaSaM
estimates motion probabilities from camera and depth ( Li et al., 2025 ) ,
MonST3R ( Zhang et al., 2025b ) and DAS3R ( Xu et al., 2024 ) predict motion
regions with reconstruction, and MoRe uses mask-guided attention ( Fang et al., 2026 ) . These methods usually define masks per frame or sequence
to support reconstruction. We make the source–target pair the basic input;
our geometry-pretrained encoder ( Chen et al., 2026 ) predicts camera
parameters only as an auxiliary task, without using them to compensate mask
features.

5 Limitations

blocks.en:
Boundary quality. Masks from a promptable segmenter inherit its
boundaries; ours are predicted directly and are softer along hair or clothing
of similar colour.

Uniform and repetitive surfaces. A blank wall or tiled floor looks
alike at matched and mismatched positions, so the decoder keys on the outer
edge and fills the interior inconsistently.

between the source and target frames, MoRSe may fail to detect it, yielding
missed detections.

of our training data is rendered, and its transfer is untested at scale.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced moving-region segmentation as a pair-conditioned task, using an
ordered source–target pair as the smallest unit in which motion is defined.
MoRSe decodes each source coordinate by attending to the target, separating
scene motion from camera-induced change without optical flow, point tracks, or a
separate segmentation foundation model at inference. MoRSe-5K evaluates
this distinction under three motion settings. Experiments show improved region
accuracy and background suppression over specialized motion-segmentation and
scene-flow baselines; real-scene supervision and small displacements remain
open.

blocks.en:
Five mask sources are curated from public video. DAVIS 2017, MoCA-Mask, OVIS,
YouTube-VOS 2019, and HOI4D all use their official training partitions; from
the HOI4D training split we draw a pool of 1,022 clips. A two-stage funnel
keeps 392 of 5,231 candidate clips ( 43.3 % 43.3\% of DAVIS 2017, 52.1 % 52.1\% of
MoCA-Mask, 6.4 % 6.4\% of OVIS, 5.3 % 5.3\% of YouTube-VOS 2019, 10.4 % 10.4\% of the HOI4D
pool), which is where the 41,474 frames those five contribute come from. Both stages target
the same mismatch between object-level annotation and the moving-region
definition. One failure mode is an unlabelled second mover, which places real
motion among the negatives; the other is an outlined instance that is mostly
still, which places static pixels among the positives. The first stage uses
long-baseline geometric motion consistency for DAVIS 2017 and MoCA, with IOU PRED = 0.85 \mathrm{IOU}_{\mathrm{PRED}}=0.85 , CD PRED = 0.05 \mathrm{CD}_{\mathrm{PRED}}=0.05 ,
minimum presence fraction 0.7 0.7 , and windows W = 12 / 4 W=12/4 ; OVIS and YouTube-VOS
2019 use interval-level surface-motion consistency based on IoU, surface-feature
motion, and camera-compensated centroid displacement. The second stage is
sequence-level manual review. Retained masks are used as moving-object support masks: annotated
instance pixels are positive on the source frame and other pixels are negative.
They are not treated as fine-grained annotations that identify independently
moving subregions.

An independent-error model would predict rapidly growing false-positive area as
more targets are unioned. The measured union grows much more slowly because
different targets tend to fail on the same pixels. Error therefore saturates
rather than accumulating, which makes a maximum a usable window operator.

blocks.en:
The first expansion of the target set recovers useful additional motion;
subsequent targets contribute progressively more false positives, so precision
declines while recall rises. Mean quality peaks at a modest window and then
changes little, motivating the adjacent-target protocol used in
Section 4.3 .

blocks.en:
Ambiguity in a single pair is a property of the formulation rather than a
failure: the pair is the smallest unit in which motion is defined, so an object
that returns to its start within the interval is read as not moving. Synthetic
pairs whose endpoints are individually consistent with a static
scene— occluded , ray-aligned , and returning —are excluded
from supervision for the same reason; pairing one source with several targets
widens the window when a longer observation is needed. The defect this section
illustrates is the lack of spatial coupling between decoded coordinates: the
coordinate-wise decoder is most exposed on thin structures and low-texture
support, where a single query has little local evidence to draw on.
